label: copy-phase echo of b/f/s/g at recall positions 1 or 3
explanation: Very sparse feature (~0.01% of steps). Almost all of it (99.5% of mass) falls in the copy phase, where the fed-back input is b, f, s or g (b > f, s > g; 96% of mass). It concentrates at recall_idx 1 (the input is orig(0), 49% of mass) and recall_idx 3 (38%), and in short sequences (L=3 lift 22x, L=4 lift 4x). It is almost silent in the original phase, on the delimiter, and on first occurrences. The strongest activations are L=3 sequences like f/b ? k <DEL> [f], where the next output is k. Magnitude is higher for L=3 and recall_idx 1, and higher when next_out is k, a, p, u or r. These conditions are necessary but nowhere near sufficient: the predicate gets ~0.84 recall at ~0.5% precision, and adding L or next_out conditions raises precision only at a large cost to recall (best F1 ~0.18). The extra selectivity seems to depend on hidden-state or context details that the available variables do not capture.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=7: b, s, f, g; t=5: f, s, g, b; t=4: f, b, g, s) and the token being output (most: u, b, a, n, r, w; least: x, v, m, h); timing cues that raise it most: L=3 & t=4, recall_idx=3, L=4 & t=7.
